A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAnchors work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional sensitivity material in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original runtime, sampling, precision, coverage, and explanation-length measurements across tabular, text, and image experiments in Section 4 and the appendix figures.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds Gemma evaluations, parameter-sensitivity results, and measured memory usage.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 and the HT/VT definitions are unchanged. However, v3 Section 3.4 newly mentions removing low-contribution predicates through light sampling between HT and VT. This step appears in neither version's pseudocode, leaving uncertain whether the procedure changed or an existing implementation detail was newly disclosed.

E1.justification: Section 4.5 adds actual evaluations on SST-2 and AG News, substantially extending text-data coverage beyond the original RT-Polarity evaluation. The Adult, RT-Polarity, and ImageNet-subset studies remain. Preparation and detailed task settings for the added datasets are only sparsely documented.

E2.justification: Original Anchors remains the evaluated comparison method, including in the added evaluations. RF, NN, GBT, Llama, YOLOv8, and Gemma are models being explained, not competing explanation methods. Newly discussed related methods are not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated Llama target from Llama 2-7B to Llama 3-8B without establishing that experiments were rerun. v3 also adds Gemma-2-2B configurations and a memory-usage comparison excluding model and dataset memory. Existing dataset counts, default thresholds, and original evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 mentions grid search for selecting defaults but provides no sensitivity results. v3 Section 4.4 and Appendix C report joint threshold sweeps examining runtime, coverage, and explanation length across representative models. Section 3.5 additionally evaluates memory overhead. Existing cold-start and fidelity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report shuffle seed 42, mean ± 95% confidence intervals in Table 2, and the same distribution plots. No new repeated-run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are reported. The added Gemma and memory summaries provide no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds Gemma speedups of 4.56× on SST-2 and 2.91× on AG News, with sampling reductions of 78% and 66%, respectively. It also adds sensitivity results and average memory usage of 279.97 MB versus 276.81 MB for Anchors. Table 2 and existing plots retain their values; the changed Llama attribution does not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Definition 2.2 corrects the conditional perturbation distribution by adding normalization and requiring positive coverage. v3 also corrects the tabular input domain to a Cartesian product and clarifies rule-set notation. Sections 3.4–3.5 add an n1n2 similarity-evaluation bound and O(md) + O(m) + O(mℓ) storage analysis; the original time-complexity analysis remains.

C1.justification: The main contribution remains cached intermediate-rule reuse through horizontal and vertical transformations to accelerate Anchors while preserving explanation quality. The highlighted model-specific claim changes: the introduction assigns the retained 8.74× speedup and 87% sampling reduction to Llama 3-8B instead of Llama 2-7B, with corresponding changes in the conclusion.

C2.justification: Beyond v2's existing retrieval-quality tradeoff, v3 explains how poorly aligned HT predicates require additional VT predicates. It explicitly acknowledges limitations of rule length as an understandability proxy, discusses offline cache deployment, and adds applicability qualifications and future work in Section 6.

D1.justification: v3 newly describes cache contents, post-HT filtering through light sampling, and the parameter ranges displayed in Appendix C. Hardware, the approximately 300-hour runtime, default thresholds, and shuffle seed were already disclosed in v2. The added Gemma experiments receive little implementation detail.

R1.justification: Section 5 replaces the TreeSHAP/AcME acceleration discussion with stochastic amortization, substantially revises its account of Mor et al., and adds positioning against ReX, temporal-logic Anchors, ConLUX, and Lopardo et al. (2023). These changes broaden the distinction between MAnchors, attribution acceleration, and complementary Anchor extensions.

P1.justification: v3 polishes the abstract, introduction, and explanatory prose, standardizes understandability terminology, and adds sensitivity, additional-LLM, and limitations sections plus Appendix C. These are localized expansions and edits; the overall narrative order and most method exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the multipanel sensitivity Figure 4. All six existing figures retain identical graphic content; the earlier appendix Figures 4–6 become Figures 5–7. Figure 3 is relocated, several captions are clarified, and publication headers are corrected while the table structures and two-column layout remain.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical correctness through the normalized conditional distribution and strengthens support for parameter choices and cache costs with new analyses. Broader empirical coverage and clearer limitations also help. These gains are limited by sparse documentation of the added experiments and the unexplained reassignment of unchanged Llama results to a different model, preventing a stronger overall assessment.
